question: Let 8 be the variance of a data set. If each observation is multiplied by a constant 2 and a constant 3 is added to each observation. then the variance of the new data set is:
solution:
The correct answer is** 32.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Variance and Data Transformation:

__
 
• Variance measures the spread of a set of data points.
 
• When each observation in a data set is multiplied by a constant, the variance is multiplied by the square of that constant.
 
• Adding a constant to each observation does not change the variance.
 
• Given the original variance is 8, multiplying each observation by 2 will multiply the variance by 22=4" id="MathJax-Element-555-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">22=422=4" id="MathJax-Element-146-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">22=422=4
 22=4
 2² = 4 .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Let's calculate the new variance step-by-step:

 
• **Step 1:** Original variance = 8.
 
• **Step 2:** Multiply each observation by 2: New variance = 8×4=32" id="MathJax-Element-556-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">8×4=328×4=32" id="MathJax-Element-147-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">8×4=328×4=32

 8 \times 4 = 32 .
 
• **Step 3:** Adding a constant (3) to each observation does not change the variance.
 
• **Step 4:** The final variance remains 32.

***Hence, the variance of the new data set is 32.***
